title: Object Equality and Value Objects
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of object equality and value objects in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply object equality and value objects in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to objects representing domain values and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn Object Equality and Value Objects through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding object equality and value objects helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Object Equality and Value Objects helps you reason about implementing ==. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Implementing ==. Then connect it to Equality and hash consistency. The remaining syllabus points—Objects representing domain values—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Example: Object Equality and Value Objects
content_blocks.code:
class Tag
  attr_reader :name
  def initialize(name) = (@name = name)
  def ==(other) = other.is_a?(Tag) && name == other.name
end
puts Tag.new("ruby") == Tag.new("ruby")
